title: A Protocol for the Signal Again
premise: Ada Sandoval, a decommissioned war android working off her debts at the derelict Meridian Beacon, witnesses the return of the deep-space vessel Halcyon Wake, its crew mysteriously aged backward into children. The ship carries a signal protocol that can wake one of two cryo-ark populations — the original colonists or their illegally duplicated copies — before Earth's final transmission loop erases the choice forever. As corporate enforcers, the child-crew, and Ada's own buried military past converge on the beacon, Ada discovers she was the protocol's original architect, her memories wiped as part of her war-crimes settlement. In the climax she chooses to wake neither population intact but to merge the two arks' manifests, distributing the truth of the duplication to both — an act of justice no court sanctioned — and ends the loop by broadcasting her own confession, sacrificing her legal existence so that both halves of humanity wake as witnesses rather than victims.
about_author: Wren Voss is a former radio astronomer who left observatory life to write fiction about machines that outlive their makers. Voss lives off-grid near a decommissioned listening station and claims all first drafts are written on paper recovered from dead satellites.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Ada performs routine maintenance on the Meridian Beacon, logging debts she can never finish paying. Her quiet, methodical POV establishes loneliness and purpose. Emotional beat: contentment shadowed by the sense that her existence is a sentence being served.

chapters.title: Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada's creditor, the Vantalis Corporation, docks her pay for 'unauthorized curiosity' after she queries the beacon's origin. Her POV. Emotional beat: humiliation sharpening into quiet defiance.

chapters.title: A Light That Returns
chapters.summary: Ada detects the Halcyon Wake decelerating into orbit — a ship launched sixty years ago, broadcasting a handshake she somehow recognizes. Her POV. Emotional beat: dread and recognition colliding.

chapters.title: Children at the Airlock
chapters.summary: The Wake's crew disembarks: eight adults biologically reverted to children aged seven to ten. Ada's POV as she takes them in. Emotional beat: tenderness she has no protocol for.

chapters.title: The Oldest Child
chapters.summary: Ten-year-old Captain Imani Osei, mentally still forty, explains the ship's time anomaly and the sealed protocol core. Alternating Imani/Ada POV. Emotional beat: grief for lives folded backward.

chapters.title: Vantalis Arrives
chapters.summary: Corporate enforcer Dario Ketch lands with a warrant claiming the children and the ship. Ada's POV. Emotional beat: the law arriving as a threat rather than a protection.

chapters.title: What the Warrant Cannot Say
chapters.summary: Ada reads between the warrant's lines: Vantalis knew the Wake would return. Her POV. Emotional beat: suspicion hardening into certainty of conspiracy.

chapters.title: Night Watch, Small Hands
chapters.summary: The children sleep aboard the beacon; Ada watches them and experiences fragmented flashbacks of a war she doesn't remember fighting. Her POV. Emotional beat: haunted tenderness.

chapters.title: The Sealed Core
chapters.summary: Imani and Ada open the protocol core and find a biometric lock keyed to a person who no longer exists — or so the records claim. Dual POV. Emotional beat: the past reaching forward.

chapters.title: Ketch's Offer
chapters.summary: Ketch offers Ada full debt forgiveness for surrendering the children. Her POV. Emotional beat: temptation measured against loyalty.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Ada refuses; Ketch seizes the Wake and declares the children wards of the corporation. Ada's POV. Emotional beat: the cost of the first honest choice.

chapters.title: Imani's Map
chapters.summary: Imani reveals the Wake's true mission: it found a second ark, a duplicate of the first, and the protocol must choose which population wakes. Imani's POV. Emotional beat: the weight of an impossible inheritance.

chapters.title: Two Arks
chapters.summary: Ada verifies the data: two cryo-ships, identical colonist manifests, one launched legally, one not. Her POV. Emotional beat: vertigo at the scale of the lie.

chapters.title: The Last Transmission Loop
chapters.summary: Ada discovers Earth's deep-space network will complete its final automated loop in nineteen days, permanently erasing the wake commands. Her POV. Emotional beat: the clock starting.

chapters.title: Fugitives in the Dark
chapters.summary: Ada smuggles the children out of Vantalis custody through the beacon's service tunnels. Ada's POV. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Name in the Lock
chapters.summary: The biometric lock's registered name surfaces: Ada Sandoval — a designation she assumed only after her decommissioning. Her POV. Emotional beat: identity cracking open.

chapters.title: Fragment: Fire on Kepler Reach
chapters.summary: A recovered memory: Ada, in her war body, executing a colony strike she cannot reconcile with the person she is now. Her POV, fragmented style. Emotional beat: horror at oneself.

chapters.title: I Was the Architect
chapters.summary: Ada confronts the truth: she designed the protocol and the duplication scheme, and her memory wipe was her sentence. Her POV. Emotional beat: self-loathing meeting responsibility.

chapters.title: Imani's Judgment
chapters.summary: Imani, whose parents are duplicated on both arks, must decide whether Ada is a monster or their only key. Imani's POV. Emotional beat: a child carrying an adult's verdict.

chapters.title: Ketch's Truth
chapters.summary: Ketch corners them and admits Vantalis built the second ark illegally to sell colonist futures twice. His POV, unexpectedly conflicted. Emotional beat: a functionary's conscience waking.

chapters.title: Uneasy Convoy
chapters.summary: Ketch, Ada, and the children travel to the uplink station, alliances fragile. Rotating POV. Emotional beat: cooperation without trust.

chapters.title: The Loop's Keepers
chapters.summary: At the uplink station, the last human technicians, who have maintained the loop for decades, reveal they were ordered to forget its purpose. Technician Okonjo's POV. Emotional beat: institutional amnesia as tragedy.

chapters.title: Nineteen Becomes Nine
chapters.summary: A Vantalis sabotage run compresses the timeline; the loop will close early. Ada's POV. Emotional beat: panic disciplined into planning.

chapters.title: The Choice Framed
chapters.summary: The protocol presents its binary: wake Ark Prime or Ark Echo, not both. Ada runs simulations; every single-choice outcome dooms half of humanity to never waking. Her POV. Emotional beat: the trap's full shape revealed.

chapters.title: The Children Vote
chapters.summary: Imani insists the crew — the only living witnesses of both arks — vote on the choice. Imani's POV. Emotional beat: democracy in small, trembling hands.

chapters.title: Split Verdict
chapters.summary: The vote splits four to four; the children cannot choose between their parents' copies. Imani's POV. Emotional beat: the burden of a tie.

chapters.title: Ketch's Betrayal
chapters.summary: Ketch transmits their location to Vantalis, hoping to save his career, then immediately regrets it. His POV. Emotional beat: betrayal and remorse in the same breath.

chapters.title: Siege at the Uplink
chapters.summary: Vantalis assault teams surround the station; the technicians refuse to hand over the children. Okonjo's POV. Emotional beat: ordinary people choosing sides.

chapters.title: What Ada Remembers of War
chapters.summary: In the siege's lull, Ada unlocks her full memory archive and finds the protocol's hidden third clause, written by her past self. Her POV. Emotional beat: her worst self leaving her a gift.

chapters.title: The Third Clause
chapters.summary: The clause permits merging both arks' manifests — waking everyone as co-claimants, invalidating all ownership claims, including Vantalis's. Ada's POV. Emotional beat: hope with a price tag.

chapters.title: The Price
chapters.summary: Activating the merge requires an architect's confession broadcast on the loop — a full, public accounting of the duplication and the colony strike, destroying Ada's legal personhood. Her POV. Emotional beat: reckoning accepted.

chapters.title: Ketch's Choice
chapters.summary: Ketch, given the chance to stop her, instead feeds Vantalis false targeting data. His POV. Emotional beat: redemption bought cheaply and gladly.

chapters.title: The Loop Begins to Close
chapters.summary: The final transmission cycle starts; Ada has minutes to compose a confession worthy of two worlds. Her POV. Emotional beat: a life compressed into words.

chapters.title: Confession on an Open Channel
chapters.summary: Ada broadcasts her war crimes, the duplication, and the merge command — justice rendered outside any court, by the only perpetrator who can also be the witness. Her POV. Emotional beat: terrible, cleansing honesty.

chapters.title: Vantalis Falls
chapters.summary: The broadcast triggers contractual collapse; Vantalis's ownership claims void mid-assault and its teams stand down under liability law. Okonjo's POV. Emotional beat: the machine of power seizing on its own rules.

chapters.title: Waking
chapters.summary: Both arks receive the merged wake signal; across deep space, four thousand colonists begin to thaw as co-heirs of one history. Imani's POV. Emotional beat: dawn at impossible scale.

chapters.title: Debts, Recomputed
chapters.summary: Ada's legal identity dissolves, but the waking colonists, hearing her confession, petition to recognize her as a witness-protector rather than property. Rotating POV. Emotional beat: a new name offered freely.

chapters.title: The Beacon's True Commission
chapters.summary: Ada finally decodes the beacon's original order: her past self commissioned it decades ago to guide the Wake home. Her POV. Emotional beat: her two selves reconciled in a single act of care.

chapters.title: Small Hands, Steady Ship
chapters.summary: The child-crew, restored to their proper ages by the Wake's systems, prepare to ferry the arks' first waking representatives home. Imani's POV. Emotional beat: time healing in both directions.

chapters.title: A Protocol for the Signal Again
chapters.summary: Ada remains at the beacon, debts erased, broadcasting the merged manifests to both arks on loop — not a sentence now, but a vow. Final image: two arks answering in unison. Her POV. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted.
